extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and applicants for Research Project Grants (R01/R03/R15/R21)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating NIH Research Project Grant (RPG) applications (R01, R03, R15, R21), describing the review criteria, considerations, and scoring guidance reviewers should use when critiquing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering all of the review criteria, briefly summarize the significant strengths and weaknesses of the application and state the likelihood of the project to exert a sustained powerful influence on the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise overall impact statement reflecting how the strengths and weaknesses across all criteria affect the project's potential to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03-specific evaluation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R03 small grant supports discrete, well-defined projects that realistically can be completed in two years and that require limited levels of funding. An R03 may not contain extensive detail or discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach; appropriate justification can be literature citations, other-source data, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly for pilot/feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (AREA) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the proposed project addresses AREA objectives: (1) provide support for meritorious research, (2) strengthen research environments of schools not major NIH recipients, (3) expose undergrad/grad students to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required but may be included if available. Factor the AREA program goals into the overall impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21-specific evaluation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R21 supports exploratory/developmental work investigating novel ideas, new model systems/tools/technologies with potential significant impact. R21 need not have extensive background or preliminary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus evaluation on conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to advance knowledge. Justification can be literature citations, other-source data, or investigator data; preliminary data are not required but may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how successful completion would change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventive interventions that drive the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? For Early Stage or New Investigators, do they have appropriate experience and training? For established investigators, have they demonstrated ongoing accomplishments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-PD/PI projects assess complementary and integrated expertise, leadership approach, governance, and organizational structure. See definitions: New Investigator = has not competed successfully for a substantial competing NIH research grant; Early Stage Investigator (ESI) = New/First-Time Investigator within 10 years of terminal degree or residency (extensions possible for special circumstances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether concepts/approaches/instrumentation/interventions are novel to one field or novel broadly, or whether a refinement/improvement/new application is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If early-stage, will the strategy establish feasibility and manage particularly risky aspects? For clinical research, evaluate human subjects protection plans and inclusion plans (minorities, sexes/genders, children) in terms of scientific goals and research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment and other physical resources adequate? Will the project benefit from unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional commitment and any special environmental advantages that enhance likelihood of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (non-exempt research)
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-exempt human subjects research, evaluate justification for involvement and proposed protections according to: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all criteria are adequately addressed and no concerns, write 'Acceptable Risks and/or Adequate Protections' (brief explanation advisable). If one or more are inadequate, write 'Unacceptable Risks and/or Inadequate Protections' and document issues. For clinical trials, evaluate the Data and Safety Monitoring Plan; if absent, notify SRO immediately. Indicate if plan is 'Acceptable' or 'Unacceptable' and explain if unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (exempt research)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research meeting one or more of the six exemption categories, evaluate: (1) justification for the exemption, (2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, (3) sources of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claimed exemption is not justified, indicate 'Unacceptable' and explain why. Note: acceptability/unacceptability that affects Approach should be reflected under 'Approach' and factored into the score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children (clinical research)
rubrics_metrics.description: When project involves clinical research, evaluate proposed plans for inclusion of minorities and members of both genders, and inclusion of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Law 103-43 requires inclusion of women and minorities unless clear compelling rationale. NIH requires inclusion of children (under age 21) unless scientific/ethical reasons to exclude. Assign codes and acceptability: Gender Inclusion Code (G1-G4), Minority Inclusion Code (M1-M5), Children Inclusion Code (C1-C4). For each category determine if recruitment targets are 'A' (acceptable) or 'U' (unacceptable). If 'U', consider this a weakness affecting overall score and explain reasons, especially for any 'U' codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender/Minority/Children coding scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes to classify inclusion: G1=Both genders; G2=Only women; G3=Only men; G4=Gender composition unknown. M1=Minority and nonminority; M2=Only minority; M3=Only nonminority; M4=Minority composition unknown; M5=Only foreign subjects. C1=Children and adults; C2=Only children; C3=No children included; C4=Representation of children unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate code(s) and assign 'A' or 'U' for acceptability. Note M5 indicates only foreign subjects; if both foreign and U.S. subjects are used, use codes 1-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals according to: (1) proposed use and species/strains/ages/sex/numbers; (2) justifications for use and appropriateness of species/numbers; (3) adequacy of veterinary care; (4) procedures for limiting discomfort, distress, pain and injury including use of analgesics/anesthetics or comfortable restraints; (5) methods of euthanasia and reason if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Vertebrate Animals checklist for additional information to determine 'Acceptable' or 'Unacceptable'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether adequate protection is proposed and flag any biosafety concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a Resubmission application (formerly amended), evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of responses to prior critiques and whether changes address earlier concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a Renewal application (formerly competing continuation), consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate accomplishments and productivity relative to the previously funded aims and whether renewal is justified by progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a Revision application (formerly competing supplement), consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Revision relates to a line of investigation previously not recommended, consider whether responses to prior comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are evident. See NIH guidance on Revision Applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the project presents special opportunities through unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and are not readily available in the U.S. or that augment U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers do not need to comment on the foreign component of domestic applications here; comments relevant to scientific approach should appear under 'Approach' (scored criterion #4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the Select Agents section including: (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used, (2) registration status of entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, (3) procedures to monitor possession/use/transfer of Select Agents, (4) plans for biosafety, biocontainment, and security of Select Agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate completeness and adequacy of select agents information and refer to Select Agents policy for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing, are reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reasonableness of data/model sharing plans where applicable; see specific items below (Data Sharing Plan, Model Organism Sharing, GWAS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Sharing Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications requesting more than $500,000 direct costs in any year are expected to include a data sharing plan. Some Program Announcements may request a plan regardless of cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reasonableness of the plan or the rationale for not sharing research data and refer to NIH Data Sharing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing Model Organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: All NIH grant applications are expected to include a plan for sharing and distributing unique model organism research resources generated using NIH funding, or state why sharing is restricted or not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model organism sharing plans are expected even if direct costs are below $500,000; evaluate adequacy of plan or justification for restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) data submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications/proposals that include GWAS are expected to include as part of the Research Plan either a plan for submission of GWAS data to the NIH designated repository or an explanation for why submission is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of the plan or justification for non-submission regardless of requested costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether resources requested are appropriate and necessary for the proposed work; see NIH Budget Information for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to offer constructive suggestions, identify critical weaknesses that must be addressed, and advise whether resubmission without fundamental revision is appropriate.
